descriptions.text: The Kipseli Router contract on Base was exploited via Improper Validation / Decimal Mismatch. The router blindly used the amount returned by an external USDC-only quoter as the raw transfer amount for tokenOut without verifying that the output token matched the quote token. The attacker used an unsupported path (e.g., WETH → cbBTC), causing the quoter to return a USDC-scaled value (6 decimals) which was then transferred as cbBTC (8 decimals), resulting in massive over-transfer. The attacker swapped only ~0.04 WETH for ~0.926 cbBTC (worth ~$72.35K). Afterward, the finder contacted the team, returned 80% of the funds as a white-hat disclosure, and kept 20% as a bug bounty.

Kipseli's PropAMM router on Base was exploited on April 22, 2026. The attacker swapped 0.04 WETH for approximately 0.93 cbBTC, exploiting a pricing logic flaw that used a USDC-denominated quote as a cbBTC transfer. The loss, reported around $72,350, resulted from missing input validation and decimal mismatch. The PropAMM router failed to verify that the quoted token matched the swap's output token. It used a USDC-scale quote when sending cbBTC, allowing the attacker to receive much more cbBTC than intended.
